title: Clinical outcome and implant survival after knee TEP implantation or knee TEP use of cemented and uncemented stems
summary: The implantation of the total knee arthroplasty (KTEP) is an established and successful procedure worldwide for knee osteoarthritis with exhausted conservative therapeutic measures. It may be necessary for initial implantations, and even more so for replacement operations, to achieve a higher degree of stabilization by installing so-called stems. Stem systems are cone systems that are coupled directly to the implant and protrude into the medullary canal of the bone shaft. Stem systems can be totally cemented, hybrid cemented (cementation of the prosthesis with uncemented pressfit stems) or, in rare cases, completely uncemented. In this study, patients who were treated with so-called uncemented and cemented stems during a first implantation or replacement operation of a total knee endoprosthesis should now be interviewed in order to investigate the implant survival and the revision rate.
conditions: Presence of a knee joint prosthesis

interventions.name: In this group the implant survival and the revision rate of the knee arthroplasty with cemented stems are examined.
In this group the implant survival and the revision rate of the knee arthroplasty with uncemented stems are examined.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Male or female patients aged ≥ 18 years
- Performed primary KTEP implantation or KTEP replacement operation using uncemented or cemented femoral or tibial stems
Exclusion criteria:
- Another revision of the knee TEP with replacement of individual or all components
